title: Coverage Options & Compliance Pathways
subtitle: How to obtain health care, and how to satisfy the requirement with $0 earned income

sections.title: 1. Decision tree — test the options in this order

c: Is the person a specified excluded individual? (WIC §14005.69(b)(2) / 42 CFR §435.554) — e.g. caregiver of a dependent child age 13 or under; in California also caregiver of an individual with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation; medically frail; 100%-rated disabled veteran; AI/AN including California Indian; foster or former foster youth under 26; in a SNAP household and not exempt from a SNAP work requirement; compliant with CalWORKs/TANF work rules; in drug or alcohol treatment; inmate or released within 90 days; pregnant or postpartum.
No work requirement applies at all. Apply for or keep Medi-Cal.

Is a mandatory exception met? (§435.553 / WIC §14005.69(f)) Under 19; entitled to or enrolled for Medicare Part A, or enrolled for Part B; described in a mandatory categorically-needy group under §1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(I)–(VII); inmate at any point in the prior 3 months.
Is MAGI household income ≤ 138% FPL? For a household of 1 in 2026: $22,025 / year ($1,836 / month).
Medi-Cal (MAGI New Adult Group, aid code M1) is the primary route — and the work requirement does apply. Go to step 4.
Income is above the Medi-Cal limit. Go to step 6 — Covered California.
Does the person meet any one of the seven compliance pathways in any single month since the last renewal?
Requirement satisfied. California needs only one qualifying month.

Is a short-term hardship event present? Inpatient-level care; Presidential emergency or disaster declaration in the county; county unemployment ≥ the lesser of 8% or 1.5× the national rate; travel outside the community for treatment of a serious or complex condition.

Do not let a notice of noncompliance lapse. 30 calendar days from receipt; Medi-Cal continues during that period; the county must first check for any other basis of eligibility and must give written notice plus fair hearing / state hearing rights. Reapplication is allowed at any time.
Federal APTC under the original §36B formula (enhancements expired 12/31/2025) plus California’s state premium subsidy up to 200% FPL for plan year 2027. ⚠ But read the PTC trap in section 3 first.
See section 7. Eligibility rules and income limits for these programs were not verified in this session — flagged F-07, values left blank.

sections.title: 2. Compliance pathways ranked for $0 earned income
sections.intro: Ranked by how well each pathway fits someone whose money comes from trading, rent and interest rather than from wages.

c: Best fit. No hours, no employer, no time-logging. DHCS tells members: “Have an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since your last renewal.” Rental income, interest and trading gains all flow into AGI and therefore into MAGI.
Measured on the MAGI-based household budget (42 CFR §435.552(f)(2); WIC §14005.69(e)(6) as amended). California requires only one qualifying month between renewals (WIC §14005.69(d)(2)).

Strong fit. Needs neither income nor hour-logging. DHCS describes half-time as “usually two or three classes, or about six to eight credits each semester”. California Community Colleges make this low-cost.

Enrollment status is determined by the school or institution. Qualifying programs: institution of higher education (20 U.S.C. 1001); career and technical education (20 U.S.C. 2302(5)); a high school; or a State-approved high-school-equivalence program. Status continues through vacation and recess. Less-than-half-time: credit hours × 3 × 4.33.
Good fit if time is available, but the program requirements are strict. Informal, self-directed volunteering does not qualify.

Must be “unpaid work, completed voluntarily or because of a mandate by court order, with a structured program … for the direct benefit of the community under the auspices of public or nonprofit organizations”. The organization must provide oversight, must not serve a partisan purpose, and must track the type of activity, dates and hours, and have a point of contact who can confirm the hours.
Available at no cost through America’s Job Center of California (AJCC) under WIOA Title I.

Qualifying programs: WIOA title I; Trade Act §236 (19 U.S.C. 2296); State or political-subdivision employment and training meeting Governor-approved standards, including a Food and Nutrition Act §6(d)(4) program — but not a supervised job search or job search training program (those may be subsidiary only if less than half the required hours); DOL or VA veteran programs; Food and Nutrition Act §6(d)(4)(N) workforce partnerships.
Plausible for property management; strong if managing property for third parties for a fee. Unverified for managing your own rentals and for Kalshi trading.

“Work” = work for money, in-kind work for goods or services, and unpaid work other than community service. CMS: self-employment from “starting a business, owning a business, or as an independent contractor” meets the definition and “the hours the individual spends performing these duties would count toward meeting the 80-hour requirement.”
Useful backstop. If a month’s income is below $580 the county may convert income to hours and add community service, work program or less-than-half-time education hours.
Income ÷ $7.25 = hours. Then hours are added together. A State may not combine education hours with another activity when the person is already enrolled at least half-time.
Probably NOT available to a full-time trader or full-time property manager.

Requires being a “seasonal worker” under 26 U.S.C. §45R(d)(5)(B) — one who “performs labor or services on a seasonal basis as defined by the Secretary of Labor, including workers covered by 29 CFR 500.20(s)(1) and retail workers employed exclusively during holiday seasons.” Flagged F-05.

sections.title: 3. ⚠ The critical trap — losing Medi-Cal for noncompliance also kills the Marketplace subsidy
sections.intro: This is the highest-impact finding on the site. It converts a paperwork failure into a full-premium problem.

c: “An individual who is eligible for Medicaid coverage that provides MEC is generally not eligible for advance payments of the premium tax credit (APTC) and premium tax credits (PTC) used to pay for coverage on a Health Insurance Exchange. Under section 1902(xx)(7)(B) of the Act, an individual is deemed to be eligible for MEC if the individual would have been eligible for Medicaid but for their failure to meet community engagement requirements. As such, an applicable individual who does not demonstrate community engagement and would otherwise be eligible for Medicaid is precluded from eligibility for APTC and PTC.”
California says the same thing to members in writing

“If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance.”

Analysis: losing Medi-Cal is normally a qualifying life event for a Marketplace special enrolment period with subsidies. For a work-requirement loss it is not. The person could end up uninsured and paying full premium — and would also face the California individual-mandate penalty for months without minimum essential coverage.

California’s county must, before denying or disenrolling, “Determine whether there is any other basis for eligibility for the Medi-Cal program or for another insurance affordability program” and must “Provide written notice and grant the individual an opportunity for a fair hearing.” And: “You can re-apply for Medi-Cal again at any time.”
Coverage still continues during the cure period

The State “must continue to provide an enrolled beneficiary with medical assistance during the 30-day period.” California: “Continue to provide the applicable individual with Medi-Cal services during the 30-calendar-day period.”

sections.title: 4. Covered California — verified current state of subsidies

c: Expired December 31, 2025. Covered California: “Before, many people had extra financial help through Enhanced Premium Tax Credits, but that help ended on Dec. 31, 2025. Monthly costs may be higher now, but some plans still cost as little as $10 per month, depending on your plan choice and income.”

The original §36B formula and the 400% FPL cap are back in force. “The PTC will continue after 2025. There is no sunset provision applicable to authorization for the credit itself. The expiration applies only to the temporary provision that expanded income eligibility and enhanced subsidy amounts … the maximum income limit of 400% of the FPL would be reinstated and the applicable percentages would revert to higher levels.”
Reinstated for enrollees with household income at or below 165% FPL; preserves IRA-level premium subsidies up to 150% FPL. Funding $190 million.

Expanded to 200% FPL. “Gov. Newsom and the California Legislature increased the amount of state funds available for the Covered California State Subsidy Program, appropriating $300 million in Health Care Affordability Reserve Fund (HCARF), up from $190 million. As a result, Californians with incomes up to 200 percent of the federal poverty level in 2027 ($31,920 for an individual or $66,000 for a family of four) will be eligible for financial help to lower the cost of monthly premiums.” Adopted under Budget Act of 2026, item 4800-101-3381.

“1. Preserves IRA-level premium subsidies for the lowest-income Covered California enrollees up to 150 percent FPL, meaning they can choose from two Silver-tier plans for $0 premium. 2. Increases the amount of premium assistance for individuals with income between 150% and up to 165% FPL relative to the 2026 program. 3. Expands eligibility to individuals up to 200% FPL.”

“over 1.9 million Californians signed up for or renewed their insurance during the 2026 open-enrollment period. This year, 235,055 Californians newly selected a health plan for 2026 and a record of nearly 1.7 million Californians renewed … bringing Covered California’s overall enrollment to a near-record high of 1,927,371 enrollees.”
“Beginning with the 2026 tax year (filed in 2027), people who get too much financial help may need to pay back the full amount they owe. It will no longer be capped based on income.”

“Effective Date: Jan. 1, 2028 — You’ll need to prove that you qualify for financial help before you get it. Financial help won’t be applied while your information is being reviewed or updated. If you don’t confirm or update your information, you won’t be automatically re-enrolled with financial help for the next plan year.”
“Effective Date: Jan. 1, 2027 — Only certain immigrant groups, like lawful permanent residents (green card holders), will be eligible for financial help to help pay for their insurance.”

“Effective Date: Jan. 1, 2026 — Bronze plans and the minimum coverage (catastrophic) plan through Covered California now count as high-deductible health plans (HDHPs) that let you contribute to a Health Savings Account (HSA).”
“While federal rules around gender-affirming care under the Affordable Care Act have changed, California law requires all Covered California plans to continue covering these services.”

BLANK — not verified. The official IRS Revenue Procedure setting 2027 applicable percentages was not retrieved in this session. Third-party summaries circulate figures, but none is published here. See flagged item F-08.

sections.title: 5. California individual mandate — why being uninsured costs money

c: “Beginning January 1, 2020, California residents must either: Have qualifying health insurance coverage; Obtain an exemption from the requirement to have coverage; Pay a penalty when they file their state tax return.”

The higher of a flat amount or a percentage of household income. Flat: “Pay $950 per adult and $475 per child” (2025 amounts). Percentage: “Pay 2.5% of the amount of gross income that exceeds the filing threshold requirements based on the tax filing status and number of dependents.”
Individual making less than $57,580 → $950. Married couple under $115,146 → $1,900. Family of four (2 married adults, 2 children) under $177,163 → $2,850.

“FTB’s most recent 2025 indexing contained a rounding error for the Individual Shared Responsibility penalty amount for dependent children. The corrected penalty amount per dependent child is $475 (revised from the previously stated $450).” — Tax News Flash, March 6, 2026.
Employer-sponsored plans; coverage purchased through Covered California or directly from insurers; Medicare (Parts A and C); and most Medicaid plans.
Exemptions claimed on the state return

Income below the tax filing threshold; health coverage considered unaffordable (exceeded 7.28% of household income for the 2025 taxable year); families’ combined self-only coverage unaffordable; short coverage gap of three consecutive months or less; certain non-citizens not lawfully present; certain citizens living abroad or residents of another state or territory; members of a health care sharing ministry; members of federally recognized tribes including Alaska Natives; incarceration; a household member born or adopted during the year; a household member who died during the year; enrolled in limited or restricted-scope Medi-Cal or other DHCS coverage.
Religious conscience exemption; affordability hardship; general hardships.
FTB 3853, Health Coverage Exemptions and Individual Shared Responsibility Penalty. The amount is entered on Form 540 line 92, Form 540NR line 91, or Form 540 2EZ line 27.

BLANK — not published. FTB’s personal health-care-mandate page (last updated 09/15/2026) still shows “Sample penalty amounts for 2025”. A Covered California document titled “2026 Individual Shared Responsibility Penalty Calculation” references “$420 per month for an individual” for calendar year 2026; that figure could not be reconciled with FTB’s flat-amount method in this session and is not published as a 2026 penalty amount. See flagged item F-09.

sections.title: 6. Other coverage categories verified as relevant

c: A specified excluded individual from the work requirement (42 CFR §435.554(c)(2); WIC §14005.69(b)(2)(B)–(D), which names California Indians expressly) and exempt from six-month renewals — “Tribal members … are not subject to this rule”; they “will continue to renew annually.”

A veteran with a VA disability rated as 100 percent (total) under 38 U.S.C. §1155 is a specified excluded individual. Separately, “any employment and training program of the Department of Labor or Veterans Affairs that serves veterans must be an approved work program.”
A specified excluded individual; also exempt from six-month renewals (“pregnant members or those in the 12 months postpartum period … are not subject to this rule”).
A specified excluded individual federally (§1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(IX)) and expressly in California (WIC §14005.69(b)(2)(N)); also exempt from six-month renewals.

Not an applicable individual — the requirement reaches the MAGI adult group. But Non-MAGI Medi-Cal carries asset limits that drop from $130,000 (one person) to $21,000 on July 1, 2027, and count “more than one house or vehicle”. A property owner in this group needs a separate asset analysis.
Entitlement to or enrolment for Part A, or enrolment for Part B, is a mandatory exception — deemed compliant.
CMSP / Medi-Cal Access Program / CDPH condition-specific programs
BLANK — eligibility rules and income limits not verified in this session. See flagged item F-07.

sections.title: 7. Action checklist — each item tied to an official source

c: Confirm which Medi-Cal group you are in. The work rule applies only to the MAGI New Adult Group (aid code M1). Non-MAGI, mandatory children’s and pregnancy groups are excluded, as are restricted-scope (emergency) Medi-Cal and pregnancy-services recipients.
Determines whether the rule applies at all.

Create or update a BenefitsCal account and make sure the county has a current mailing address, telephone number and email. DHCS: “This is very important. Your county Medi-Cal office will mail, email, or text you more information about these rules.”
Notices are what start the 30-day clock; a stale address is the classic cause of avoidable coverage loss.

Watch for the DHCS outreach letter. DHCS began mailing in late August 2026; counties must include it with application materials for new and returning members October 1 – December 31, 2026. A text campaign began February 2026.
The letter explains who is subject, the exemptions, the consequences, and how to report changes.

Keep a simple monthly income record — Kalshi PnL statement and trade history, rent receipts and Schedule E figures, 1099-INT from the bank and from Kalshi. Target: at least one month with ≥ $580 of MAGI household income between renewals.
The income pathway is the lowest-paperwork route, and California needs only one qualifying month.
Line up a backup pathway now — half-time enrolment at a California Community College, or registration at an America’s Job Center of California.
If a trading loss plus a rental vacancy leaves a month under $580, a fallback already exists.

Screen yourself for an exclusion — in particular the California category WIC §14005.69(b)(2)(F): caregiver of “an individual with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation”, which is broader than the federal ADA-disabled definition. Also (b)(2)(H)(v): a serious or complex medical condition.
Exclusions remove the requirement entirely rather than requiring monthly proof.
Never ignore a notice of noncompliance. 30 calendar days from receipt; coverage continues during that period; then request a state hearing and ask about continued aid.
A lapse costs both Medi-Cal and APTC/PTC.
Diary the renewal dates. From 2027 the New Adult Group moves to six-month redeterminations. DHCS: “If you miss deadlines, you could lose your Medi-Cal coverage.”
Missing a renewal is a separate coverage-loss risk from failing the work test.
Report income accurately on any Marketplace application. The PTC repayment cap is removed from the 2026 tax year.
Unlimited repayment exposure on a volatile MAGI.
Get tax advice before filing. Kalshi issues no information return for event-contract trading profit and the IRS characterisation is unresolved.
The AGI/MAGI number drives both Medi-Cal eligibility and the $580 test.
